w:r.w:t: TenderOS 2.1 - Global Functional Audit - Part 2
Coverage Completion
Mode: strict read-only
Executive Summary
Verdict: FUNCTIONALLY BROAD AND MOSTLY CONNECTED, BUT NOT YET A FULLY PROVEN SINGLE PRODUCTION CHAIN.

This Part 2 confirms that TenderOS now contains a real end-to-end product surface across market watch, opportunities, tenders, DCE, analysis, checklist, administrative dossier, pricing, technical memo, document generation, validation, response package, submission/export, integrations, billing and AI configuration.

The product is not a hollow shell anymore: the backend exposes dedicated controllers and use cases for each major stage, and the frontend contains corresponding protected pages and sections. That said, this audit remains a code-and-structure audit, not a full production replay. The repository demonstrates a credible business chain, but some links remain hybrid, partially parallel, or not fully proven in one frozen release snapshot.

Scope of Part 2

This report intentionally does not re-audit A1 to A6.4 in depth. CandidateCompany, CandidateEstablishment, checklist/go-no-go candidate migration and technical memo candidate identity are treated here only when they participate in the broader business workflow.
Master Product Flow - Real Coverage

1. Market Watch exists as a real entry point. Evidence: market-watch saved searches and external tenders controllers expose listing, status, matches and promote endpoints, including POST market-watch/external-tenders/:externalTenderId/promote.
2. Opportunity is a real intermediate business object. Evidence: opportunities controller supports create, list, update, status, archive, quick-score, go-no-go decisions and promote.

3. Tender is a real central aggregate. Evidence: tenders controller exposes create, list, board, stats, profile, readiness, history, checklist, criteria, requested documents, milestones, risks, alerts and candidate assignment endpoints.
4. DCE intake is real. Evidence: dce controller exposes POST tenders/:tenderId/dce, POST documents, POST import-zip, import job status, document list, update, category patch, download and delete.

5. Analysis is real and fine-grained. Evidence: analysis controller exposes analysis creation, retry/cancel, latest summary, deadlines, criteria, clauses, requirements, risks, questions, map-suggestions and revisions.

6. Consolidation exists, but as distributed features rather than one explicit consolidated module name. Evidence: analysis revisions, AI suggestion mapping, tender checklist/criteria/requested-document surfaces, cockpit/workspace UI sections.
7. Lots and requirements are real. Evidence: tender-lots controller plus tenders controller criteria and requested-documents subflows.
8. GO/NO-GO is real on both opportunity and tender paths. Evidence: opportunity go-no-go decisions and tender go-no-go report/decisions controllers.
9. Checklist is real and connected. Evidence: tenders controller checklist endpoints plus checklist-intelligence controller for AI document matching, attaching, detaching and reconcile.

10. Administrative dossier is real and deep. Evidence: administrative-dossier controllers cover dossier lifecycle, requirements, checklist, administrative documents, consortium, DC1, DC2, DUME, subcontractors, engagement act, signing powers and official-form generation/PDF flows.

11. Chiffrage is real in two layers. Evidence: pricing controller for pricing estimates and summary; pricing-schedule controllers for extracted BPU/DPGF-like workbook flows, line edits, controls, validation and final file generation.
12. Technical Memo is real. Evidence: tender-technical-memos and technical-memos controllers cover create, prepare, map, section generation, coverage, validation, edit and export.
13. Generated documents are real. Evidence: tender-document-generation and generated-documents controllers cover list, generate, regenerate and revision download.
14. Validation is real and positioned before final approval. Evidence: validation controller exposes run, get, readiness, resolve/reopen issue, final-approval and reopen.

15. Response Package is real. Evidence: tender-response-packages, response-packages and package-artifacts controllers cover create, build, qualify items, attach documents, completeness, validate, generate and download package versions.

16. Submission / final deposit is real. Evidence: submission controller exposes readiness, capabilities, start submission, create submission, proofs, receipt confirmation, replacement, withdrawal, cancel and reject.
17. Export final is real. Evidence: export controller exposes export capabilities, preview, list, get and download.
Cross-Cutting Product Coverage
Collaboration: dedicated workspace module and chat module are present in AppModule; notifications module and notification event consumers are also wired globally.

Knowledge Base / Response Library: knowledge-base module is present; generated documents, deliverables and export template surfaces show reusable content and output management rather than a single isolated editor.

Integration Hub / API Keys / Webhooks / Connectors: integrations and connectors modules are present in AppModule, with explicit webhook delivery worker and API/webhook pages under the protected frontend tree.
Billing / Quotas / Subscription: billing module, quota threshold consumers, subscription-usage module and checkout/plan catalog/entitlement override controllers are present.

AI Catalog / Routing / Benchmark: AiBenchmarkModule and RoutingPolicyBridgeModule are globally imported; ai-configuration protected routes exist for models, routing policies, recommendations, benchmarks and prompts.

Observability / Outbox / Events: OutboxModule.forRoot is the single assembly point for integration, notification and quota threshold handlers. This is a strong structural sign of product-level event flow rather than disconnected modules.

Onboarding / Organizations / Identity / Permissions: identity, organizations and memberships modules are present globally; earlier staging diagnostics already showed onboarding exists as a real product path, even if not re-executed in this Part 2.
Tenant isolation: repeated use of AuthenticatedGuard and OrganizationMembershipGuard across audited controllers strongly indicates organization scoping as a default discipline.

Audit trail: many mutation use cases emit explicit action/resourceType metadata, especially visible in pricing-schedule and other previously audited modules; the repo uses action-oriented audit patterns rather than ad hoc logs.
Storage: document download endpoints, generated artifact endpoints, DCE upload/download and connector/storage modules show storage is a first-class concern, not a mock-only concept.
What Is Strongly Confirmed
- TenderOS has a genuine multi-stage AO pipeline in code. The chain is no longer fragmented into unrelated sprint demos.
- The backend naming and controller surface mostly match the product narrative from detection to final package/export.
- AI is embedded at multiple stages: analysis, checklist suggestions, technical memo, document generation, routing and benchmark configuration.
- Billing and quota governance are not bolted on externally; they are integrated into the application module graph.
What Remains Partially Hybrid or Not Fully Proven

F1 - Full single-path unification is still not strictly proven. The repository exposes both modernized candidate flows and legacy client/company-profile dependencies. This was already true in Part 1 and remains true when viewing the full product chain.

F2 - The business chain is broad, but some transitions are product-level compositions rather than a single orchestrated saga. Example: consolidation spans analysis revisions, suggestions, checklist and workspace surfaces rather than one explicit consolidation aggregate.

F3 - DCE refresh / synchronization is only partially demonstrated by controller naming and module presence in this read-only pass. DCE intake is clear; refresh semantics need deeper targeted audit if they are critical for go-live.

F4 - Response finalization exists through validation, response package, submission and export modules, but this audit does not prove one single non-branching happy path enforced by the domain. It proves capability presence and strong product intent.
F5 - Because the worktree is dirty, this is still not a release-candidate proof. It is a structural and functional coherence audit over an in-progress integration tree.
Overall Product Answer
Can TenderOS 2.1 realistically execute an end-to-end tender workflow from detection to final dossier production on coherent sources of truth?
Answer: mostly yes at the product-architecture and functional-surface level; not yet fully yes as a zero-reserve production proof.
Why yes: every major step now exists with concrete backend endpoints and matching frontend areas. The repo reflects one product much more than a collection of isolated sprint artifacts.

Why not fully yes: some source-of-truth boundaries are still hybrid, some transitions are distributed across modules rather than enforced in a single business spine, and the current audit was performed on a dirty integration tree rather than a clean frozen candidate.
Operational Status
Status recommendation: READY FOR NEXT TARGETED GLOBAL RE-AUDITS, NOT YET READY FOR CLAIM OF COMPLETE V2.1 PRODUCT UNIFICATION WITHOUT QUALIFIERS.
Recommended Next Audit Waves
Wave P2-1: targeted deep audit of DCE refresh/synchronization and analysis re-entry behavior.
Wave P2-2: targeted deep audit of finalization chain from validated assets to response package to submission/export proof artifacts.
Wave P2-3: targeted deep audit of billing/quotas versus AI-intensive workflows under real feature gating.
Wave P2-4: clean-snapshot audit once the integration worktree stabilizes.
